name: BRCA1 and BRCA2
summary: Germline pathogenic variants in BRCA1 or BRCA2 confer hereditary breast and ovarian cancer risk and render tumours homologous recombination-deficient, predicting sensitivity to PARP inhibitors and platinum agents.
biology: BRCA1 and BRCA2 are essential for homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks; BRCA2 loads RAD51 onto resected DNA. Tumours with biallelic loss rely on error-prone repair pathways. PARP inhibition traps PARP on DNA and prevents single-strand break repair, generating replication-associated double-strand breaks that cannot be repaired, producing synthetic lethality. BRCA1-associated cancers are frequently triple-negative, whereas BRCA2-associated cancers are more often hormone receptor-positive.
alterations: Germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic BRCA1 variants
Germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic BRCA2 variants

methods: Germline genetic testing on blood or saliva (sequencing plus copy-number/large rearrangement analysis)
Tumour NGS (detects germline and somatic variants; germline confirmation required)
Genomic scar/homologous recombination deficiency assays (investigational in breast cancer)
testing.specimen: Peripheral blood or saliva for germline testing; tumour tissue for somatic testing
testing.notes: Testing should be accompanied by genetic counselling and cascade testing for relatives. Eligibility criteria for germline testing have broadened to support treatment decisions.

predictiveRelevance: Germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants predict benefit from olaparib and talazoparib in HER2-negative metastatic disease, and from adjuvant olaparib in high-risk early HER2-negative disease. They are associated with platinum sensitivity in triple-negative disease. Evidence for PARP inhibitors in somatic BRCA mutations is emerging from phase II data.
resistance: BRCA1/2 reversion mutations restoring the reading frame
Loss of 53BP1, shieldin complex or REV7 restoring end resection in BRCA1-deficient cells
cnsConsiderations: Patients with BRCA-associated triple-negative disease are at risk of brain metastases; talazoparib and olaparib have limited prospective CNS data.
